item.title: Making Parasites Glow
item.description: This is one of the blog post from my old blog that I did as part of a module in my undergrad, I’ve transfered it to my new site. For the 4th year of my MSci I’m working in the Tewari lab. A lab that specialises in understanding specific proteins, their roles and locations in Plasmodium, the group of parasites that causes malaria. One of the most useful tools used is fluorescent microscopy.

SAMUEL JAMES WINDLE sam@windle.me.uk RESEARCH INTEREST With a broad biological background from my undergrad, I am currently growing my bioinformatical skills to match. I’m motivated towards developing novel tools and techniques, solving challenges I want to be a part of a team developing novel and innovative techniques that can be applied by others. RESEARCH EXPERIENCE ANTIOMICROBIAL RESISTANCE (AMR) IN ARGENTINIAN BEEFLOTS OCTOBER 2022 – ONGOING BBSRC DTP PROJECT, DR ADAM BLANCHARD, UNIVERSITY OF NOTTINGHAM Ongoing PhD project.
